newsitem.title: USA: FBI puts murder suspect on its most-wanted list.
newsitem.headline: FBI puts murder suspect on its most-wanted list.

text.p: The FBI Thursday placed Andrew Cunanan, the suspect in a three-state killing spree, on its list of 10 most-wanted fugitives, and said it is offering a $10,000 reward for information leading to his arrest.
Cunanan, 27, the subject of an intense nationwide manhunt, has been charged with one murder in Minnesota and is wanted for questioning in three other murders in Minnesota, Illinois and New Jersey.
The FBI said it is seeking Cunanan on a federal arrest warrant charging him with unlawful flight to avoid prosecution.
Cunanan's mother, from whom he is estranged, described him in a interview with the Chicago Sun-Times last month as a "high-class homosexual prostitute."

Cunanan is suspected in the bludgeoning death of Jeffrey Trail, 28, a one-time close friend, in Minneapolis, and has been charged with the shooting death of his former lover and Minneapolis architect David Madson, 33.
The FBI said he allegedly stole Madson's Jeep Cherokee, which was later discovered in Chicago. Cunanan is a suspect in the murder of Chicago real estate tycoon Lee Miglin.
Miglin's car then was found in a cemetery parking lot in Pennsville, New Jersey, where the caretaker, William Reese, was murdered about a month ago.
The FBI said there were "strong similarities" between the various murders.

It said Cunanan, who allegedly has ties to the gay community, speaks several foreign languages and has used the alias Andrew DeSilva. He often portrayed himself as wealthy and had a flamboyant lifestyle even though he was unemployed.
The FBI said he is about 5-feet-10, weighing 160 to 180 pounds, with dark brown hair and brown eyes. Cunanan should be considered armed and dangerous.
The FBI said he became the 449th fugitive placed on its most- wanted list, which began in 1950. Of the total, 420 have been apprehended or located.
